passages.text: Men, however sharp and intellectual, however clearly they see the force of the logic that nothing here can be free, are all compelled to think they are free; they cannot help it. No work can go on until we begin to say we are free. It means that the freedom we talk about is the glimpse of the blue sky through the clouds and that the real freedom — the blue sky itself — is behind.
passages.note: Longing for freedom; glimpses of something greater

passages.text: It is not that you are going to become God or perfect; you are already perfect; and whenever you think you are not, it is a delusion.

We must always bear in mind that we are not going to be free, but are free already. Every idea that we are bound is a delusion. Every idea that we are happy or unhappy is a tremendous delusion; and another delusion will come — that we have got to work and worship and struggle to be free — and this will chase out the first delusion, and then both will stop.
passages.note: Feeling trapped; spiritual striving and freedom
